verdict.rationale: Hyperbrowser documents an explicit captcha stance: automatic CAPTCHA detection and solving, opt-in at session creation, backed by stealth and anti-detection modes. The evidence does not show what happens when solving fails, so the story's core concern of avoiding silent task failures is not covered. The single community report of being blocked by Cloudflare is about bot blocking, not a concrete failure of captcha solving, so it does not make this disputed. missing for 10: documented failure/error signaling when a CAPTCHA can't be solved, a human-in-the-loop fallback, scope of supported CAPTCHA types, independent hands-on corroboration of solving success.

support.subject: As an automation-engineer, I can rely on a documented captcha stance — automatic solving, human fallback, or explicit non-support — instead of silent task failures

citations.quote: Hyperbrowser can automatically detect and solve CAPTCHAs when you enable it during session creation.
Stealth mode applies anti-detection techniques to help your automated browser sessions bypass bot detection.
